A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SAF3R. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete Appendices A–B are readable and support reliable comparison after matching relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original camera-pose and reconstruction evaluations, efficiency measurements, attention analyses, and ablations in Section 5 and Appendices A–B.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results, including benchmark comparisons in Tables 2–4, repeated-run ablations in Table 5, and additional appendix evaluations.

M1.justification: Section 4 retains the same four sparse kernels, offline head profiling, and online Query-Probe/DINO Top-K adaptation. No algorithmic component or inference procedure changes.

E1.justification: The same tasks and datasets remain: Co3D-v2, RealEstate10K, 7Scenes, HiRoom, ETH3D, ScanNet++, DTU, and ScanNet. The Oxford Spires loop-closure case and appendix scenarios are also retained.

E2.justification: Matched comparisons retain full attention, FastVGGT, Co-Me, SparseVGGT, AVGGT, their applicable model variants, and the same kernel controls. Newly cited streaming and context-compression methods are not added as evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Section 5.1 retains the same sampling protocols, sparse and dense sequence lengths, metrics, model configurations, and comparator settings. The appendix evaluation procedures also remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Both versions contain the same profiling and kernel ablations, DINO Top-K sensitivity analysis, Oxford Spires case, attention visualizations, and sparsity–latency analysis in Section 5.3 and Appendices A–B.

E5.justification: Table 5 retains five runs using different randomly sampled image sets and identical plus/minus reporting. No run-count, seed, uncertainty-estimation, or significance-testing practice is added or revised.

E6.justification: Tables 2–10 retain their numerical entries, and the efficiency plots and qualitative findings are unchanged. For example, Table 4 still reports a 7.3× speedup for SAF3R on π3 with 700 ScanNet images.

T1.justification: The NMSE definition in Equation 1, constrained configuration selection in Equation 2, and mean-query derivation for Query-Probe Top-K remain unchanged. No formal assumption, proof, or mathematical result is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about heterogeneous attention, training-free dynamic sparsification, and acceleration while preserving pose and reconstruction quality.

C2.justification: Section 2.1 newly specifies an offline reconstruction scope, with all input views available for joint reasoning, and distinguishes it from streaming reconstruction. Existing result interpretations and DINO-related failure conditions in Sections 5.3 and 6 remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Both retain the same PyTorch/Triton implementation disclosure, ten ETH3D calibration sequences, baseline sparsity, online K settings, H100 hardware, and code-access information. No reproducibility detail is added or revised.

R1.justification: Sections 2.1 and 2.3 broaden the existing discussion with streaming reconstruction and test-time context compression, including VGG-T3, ZipMap, and Scal3R; fifteen references are added. This is a bounded expansion of the research context, with the central head-wise dynamic-sparsity positioning retained.

P1.justification: Rewriting is concentrated in Sections 2.1 and 2.3, clarifying the progression of reconstruction models and the offline/streaming distinction. The overall section sequence and remaining scientific narrative are retained.

P2.justification: Text expansion changes page composition and relocates existing displays: Figures 3–5 move to subsequent pages, and Table 3 moves from page 11 to page 12. Figure content, axes, legends, and table structures remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v2 improves contextual completeness and scope clarity by explicitly distinguishing offline from streaming reconstruction and discussing test-time context compression in Sections 2.1 and 2.3. The method, results, and appendix evidence remain unchanged, so the supported quality gain is limited to clearer applicability and research positioning.
